title: fix(issue-authoring): mechanically enforce the needs-decision label for maintainer-decision-shaped issues
body:
<!-- idd-skill-authoring-publication: target=target-8c1f160f13554a96; anchor=target-8c1f160f13554a96; set=set-68e56f14e19f7580; session=claude-idd0-30c27cd2b171; token=pub-9c0d5f13c4fe53fe -->

## Background

`audit-authored-issue.mts` mechanically enforces one score-to-label
binding: `checkSuitabilityBlockedByHuman` fails an authored body when its
autopilot-suitability marker is `1` but the resolved
`blockedByHumanLabelName` (default `status:blocked-by-human`) is not among
the `--label` values passed in. There is no equivalent mechanical check for
the `needsDecisionLabelName` policy key (default `status:needs-decision`) --
confirmed via `node scripts/audit-authored-issue.mjs --help` and a read of
`src/scripts/audit-authored-issue.mts`: the only cross-field label check in
the file is the suitability-1 one. `needsDecisionLabelName` itself already
exists as a first-class policy key -- `discover-orphan-filter.mts` reads and
filters on it identically to `blockedByHumanLabelName` -- so the gap is
narrow: the config plumbing is already shared, only the authoring-time
enforcement is missing.

In practice this repository's own precedent chain of "no single proposed
change, a maintainer must pick an option" issues is inconsistent about
carrying `status:needs-decision` at publish time. Checked directly:

| Issue | `status:needs-decision` at any point | Applied how |
| ----- | ------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| #2181 | yes | (not re-verified for this table's timing column) |
| #2377 | yes | applied 2s after issue creation (`kurone-kito`, automated) |
| #2567 | yes | applied 2s after issue creation (`kurone-kito`, automated) |
| #2631 | yes | present from creation |
| #2636 | no (until manually applied during this retrospective's parent session) | -- |
| #2637 | no (until manually applied during this retrospective's parent session) | -- |

#2377 and #2567's timeline events (`gh api .../issues/<n>/timeline`) show
`status:needs-decision` landing 2 seconds after issue creation, both
attributed to the same authenticated actor used by this repository's IDD
automation -- i.e. an established, scripted-or-disciplined authoring-time
practice, not an ad hoc human label click. #2636 and #2637 were published
without it and without a body-level structural marker recording their
bucket at all, so a later Discover/A4.5 pass had to independently re-derive
"this is needs-decision-shaped" by reading the full body before it could
apply the label -- exactly the redundant re-derivation cost the existing
`autopilot-suitability` footer marker was introduced to avoid for the
*suitability* axis (`docs/issue-authoring-skill.md`'s "Autopilot-suitability
score" section: "so the Discover phase can rank and route candidates by a
cheap read instead of re-deriving autonomy per candidate"). The same
rationale applies to the *readiness bucket* axis and currently has no
mechanical backstop.

This is a distinct gap from kurone-kito/idd-skill#2621 (currently open, PR
#2628): #2621 mechanically verifies that an *owner-marker/publication-token*
trail exists on an authoring-labeled issue -- a provenance/concurrency-safety
concern. This issue is about a completely orthogonal signal: whether a
*readiness-bucket* determination the authoring flow already made gets
mechanically reflected in a durable label, independent of whether the
marker trail is present or valid.

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: the right mechanical signal for "this body is
needs-decision-shaped" involves a real reliability tradeoff between a new
structural marker and free-text pattern matching, and is a maintainer
call.

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Add a dedicated hidden marker.** Introduce
   `<!-- {markerPrefix}-authoring-bucket: ready|deferred|needs-decision|blocked-by-human|out-of-scope -->`
   as a body footer emitted at authoring time (mirroring the existing
   `autopilot-suitability` marker's footer convention exactly). Add
   `checkSuitabilityNeedsDecision` to `audit-authored-issue.mts`, reusing
   the already-existing `needsDecisionLabelName` policy key exactly as
   `checkSuitabilityBlockedByHuman` reuses `blockedByHumanLabelName`:
   fail when the marker reads `needs-decision` but the label is absent
   from `--label`. Most robust and consistent with the repository's
   existing marker vocabulary; requires authoring flow changes plus a
   backfill decision for the pre-existing precedent chain (#2181/#2377/
   #2567/#2631, all already compliant, and #2636/#2637, not yet).
2. **Detect the existing free-text convention instead.** The precedent
   chain already shares a consistent phrase ("No single proposed change:
   this is a maintainer decision...") in the `## Proposed change`
   section. A regex-based check could flag a body matching that shape
   without the label present, with no new marker to emit or maintain.
   Cheaper to retrofit onto the existing backlog, but fragile to
   phrasing drift and both false positives (a `ready` issue that
   happens to use similar wording) and false negatives (a
   needs-decision issue phrased differently).
3. **Document the practice only, no mechanical check.** Add the binding
   rule to `contract.md`'s "Readiness buckets" or "Autopilot-suitability
   score" section as prose guidance, mirroring the score-1 rule's
   wording, without linter enforcement. Cheapest, but this issue's own
   evidence (#2636/#2637 slipping past an established practice with no
   mechanical backstop) suggests prose alone does not reliably hold once
   a session is time-pressured or working across many issues in one
   pass.
4. **Something else the maintainer prefers** -- for example scoping
   option 1's marker to only the two axis values that currently have
   real behavioral consequences (`needs-decision` and `blocked-by-human`,
   folding blocked-by-human's existing suitability-1 binding into the
   same marker) rather than all five buckets.

Whichever option is chosen, keep the config plumbing shared: do not
introduce a second, differently-named policy key for the same
`needsDecisionLabelName` concept `discover-orphan-filter.mts` already
resolves.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer states which option above to take (or a different
      resolution) in a comment on this issue.
- [ ] Close this issue once that decision is recorded. The chosen option
      becomes a follow-up `ready` issue scoped to the exact
      marker/check/doc change, including a backfill decision for the
      existing precedent-chain issues.

## Candidate files

- `skills/issue-authoring/references/contract.md` (canonical source)
- `.claude/skills/issue-authoring/references/contract.md` (generated
  mirror, via `node scripts/sync-docs.mjs --apply` if the canonical doc
  changes)
- `docs/issue-authoring-skill.md`
- `src/scripts/audit-authored-issue.mts`
- `tests/audit-authored-issue.test.mts`

---

_Autopilot suitability: 3 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented. This is a policy/design
tradeoff between a new marker, free-text detection, and prose-only
guidance for the same enforcement gap; the factual evidence above
(the existing checkSuitabilityBlockedByHuman precedent, the shared
needsDecisionLabelName config key, and the #2377/#2567 vs #2636/#2637
inconsistency) is settled and does not need re-deriving._
